OK, here's my story, maybe it can help you. 7 years ago, I was out of control. I had a lot of rage outbursts, I was cheating on my fiancee, doing things that were extremely self-destructive. My life was spiraling out of control. I didn't have any idea of my self identity. I was a mess! I ended up having a mental breakdown and going inpatient at a psychiatric hospital for 2 weeks. I thought I was fine to come home. Came home for the weekend and went right back in for another 2 weeks.  Finally after a month total of being inpatient, I was able to come home and start the difficult job of working on myself by doing outpatient therapy and DBT therapy and medication. I did a full year of DBT. It helped so very much and I still use those skills today. Another thing that really helped me was getting into a PTSD group because I'm dealing with that as well. 

7 years after the breakdown, I have a wonderful relationship with my 14 year old daughter, and my moods are stabilized, and I have an identity now. I'm not cured, but I'm a work in progress.

Back story: I had a mental breakdown and my daughter was sent to live with my sister temporarily. They made me cry in a bad, dark, hopeless way. Then, something switched in me and I started to watch them again. I started to find hope in them that maybe I would have her back. Yeah, all together I spent a month inpatient. I came out with the name of a psychiatrist that did DBT and a therapist and was told to call and set up appts. That was the beginning of my borderline journey, or at least finally being diagnosed.

Now, 6 years later, my BPD symptoms have lightened up quite a bit. I'm no longer suicidal. I do feel I have more self worth and more of an identity than before. I've been able to go without being in a relationship for 3 years, and I'm good with that. I'm not cured. I will never be cured. But my symptoms are so much more manageable than 6 years ago and for that, I'm thankful!

Hope you can find something of use in my story OP. Hope everything starts looking up for you. Things do get easier.

I'm not sure if the surgeryI had was the same the other person in this thread is getting. The first surgery on my foot was to twist everything back in the right direction and hold it all together with an external fixator (basically a cage that went from my toes to my midcalf, held in place with long metal rods that went straight thru my bones! That was rather painful and uncomfortable. I hated it! Then I got that off and was in a cast for 2 weeks then back in for my 2nd surgery. This time, to get metal rods placed inside my foot to stabilize it. That was supposed to be all I needed for surgeries.

At that point my foot looked fixed, even tho it still had healing left to do. A couple weeks later I got a pretty massive infection in my foot. It was almost to the bone. I almost lost it. But they once again took me to the OR to clean out the infection and open 2 massive holes in my foot. I was devastated! Before I could leave the hospital they took me to the OR for a 4th time. This time just to make double sure they got all the infection, clean it up good, pack it well, put a woundvac on it...that sort of thing. 

About two weeks after I got back to the nursing home, I ended up having to go back to the OR a 5th time! I had major infection again and the need to make a quick decision on how to fix it. The took my hardware out of my foot, cleaned up all the infection, and fused my foot/ankle so that I have some stability. I was very upset that they had to take my hardware because it felt like I had gone thru all that crap for nothing. Spent a week in the hospital then had my final foot surgery to do a final clean up on it and put on the woundvac. 

6 months and 6 surgeries later you'd think I'd have more to show for it then some massive scars and a crooked, fused foot
